data.text_8: The Young Black Nameless Coalition was born from a simple, radical idea: that the people historically erased from power deserve a platform built in their name. We organize, advocate, document, and amplify — because representation without action is just performance.
data.text_9: We center the experiences of young Black individuals in every decision we make. From street-level advocacy to policy change, from community care to political organizing — YBNC exists at the intersection of where movement-building actually happens.
data.text_10: "We will be here every day and every night until we see some justice. The support in the comments is not the same as tangible support in the form of showing up."

data.text_11: Ashley Dorelus is a documentary filmmaker, social justice advocate, and community organizer based in Vallejo, California. She has been on the frontlines since May 29, 2020 — traveling to over 20 states and dozens of cities to document the uprising at the intersection of two pandemics: COVID-19 and the ongoing genocide of Black people at the hands of police.
data.text_12: From Oakland to Minneapolis, Philadelphia to Atlanta — Ashley's lens captured what mainstream media refused to show. Her work, shared widely after Amanda Seals amplified her documentation of the Daunte Wright shooting, helped galvanize national attention to frontline journalism by community members.
data.text_13: A 🇭🇹 Haitian-American, Ashley received a Community Hero Award for her work and founded YBNC as a vehicle for turning documentation into organized, sustained action. She believes community-driven change begins with showing up.
